items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So he hired me... So he had a band. The band was what I just named: him and Nat, Sam Jones, Junior Mance, and me. We made an album called Sharpshooters.

ctx.x: [Oscar] Pettiford. Pettiford’s band. He sat in with Pettiford, and Pettiford hired him. After that he played with Pettiford a little bit. He felt his way around. I think he got in touch with John Levy and told him he wanted to have a band. So he got a band and brought some guys from Florida that he had been playing with down there. They were, I think, Junior Mance, because they were – him and Nat was in the army with Junior Mance. And Sam Jones was there. He’d been – they had been playing with Sam. So it was…

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Jimmy' in the context of 'Jimmy Jones' ('Jimmy Jones was a graduate of Kentucky State University... Jimmy and I were so tight together musically'). There is no mention of Jimmy Cobb in the transcript.

ctx.x: First time to New York – you were disappointed, I understand, with 52nd Street.

I was disappointed with the club the first day I walked into it. This little greasy looking joint, in the middle of the day, and I said, oh, no. A little bitty bandstand. The clubs we played in Chicago were much nicer clubs and better rooms than – I said, so this is New York, this is 52nd Street, and this is the Onyx Club. I thought, wow, this is a real dump. I met the owner, a very nice man. I said, okay, we’re going to be coming in there the following week, I think it was. But I was pretty – surely was…
